title: Rotate
content: ### Objective Rotate Patterns and Internal Shapes/Lines based on various references. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Rotate 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Select the Pattern or Internal Shapes/ Lines or Baselines to be rotated. → The marquee box appears around the selected item. 3. Click and drag the rotate point on top of the marquee box. → The selected item rotates towards the mouse. ※ Note: * While clicking and dragging the Pattern, Internal Shapes/Lines, or Baselines, right click to access the Rotate window. Type in the desired angle, then click OK. The selected item rotates based on the entered value (ver3.2.0). #### Clockwise/Counterclockwise 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. 3. When the pop-up menu appears, select Clockwise (45º) or Clockwise (90º) or Counterclockwise (45º) or Counterclockwise (90º) → The selected pattern rotates according to the chosen options. #### X/Y Axis 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. 3. When the pop-up menu appears, select X-Axis or Y-Axis. 4. Select the line of a Pattern which should be rotated to the chosen axis. → The selected Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines are rotated to X-Axis or Y-Axis on the basis of the selected line. #### Parallel To 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. 3. When the pop-up menu appears, select Parallel to... 4. Select the line of any Patterns or Internal Lines/Shapes in the 2D window which the previously selected Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines are rotated to. This line acts as a fiducial line. → The selected line turns red. 5. Then, select the line of the rotating Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines that will rotate parallel to the fiducial line selected above. → The Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines rotates parallel to the fiducial line.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for rotating patterns and internal shapes/lines in a 2D design environment using various methods and tools.

title: Fold Pattern
content: ### Objective Use this function to create a pressing effect by adjusting the angle of Pattern's Internal Line, for instance, pressed lines of formal trousers, fold direction of pleats. ### Location Pattern Property Editor ▶ Fold ▶ Fold Angle ### Operation 1. Click on an Internal Line with Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Pattern Property Editor ▶ Fold ▶ Fold Angle 3. Adjust the value of Fold Angle as desired. ※ Note: Fold Strength | Sets the angle closer as the value increases. The value range is in between 0 to 20. ---|--- Fold Angle | Sets the value in the range of 0˚ to 360˚, 180˚ represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0˚, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360˚. Fold Rendering | Sets whether the pleats to have soft or sharp edges according to user preference. (Only applicable if Fold Arrangement is used on an Internal line.)
content_description: This web page provides guidance on creating a pressing effect in your patterns by adjusting the Fold Angle of Internal Lines for tailored finishes like trouser pleats.

Furthermore, it can also be used when designing Garments that are connected to two avatars. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ Avatar ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ Avatar → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the Avatar to be added and click Open. → The Add Avatar window appears (ver2.4.0). 3. Select the appropriate settings and click OK to place the Avatar. ※ Note: * Add Avatar Options Placement | X | Move along the X axis (left, right) relative to the center of the 3D Window. ---|---|--- Y | Move along the Y axis (top, bottom) relative to the center of the 3D Window. Z | Move along the Z axis (front, back) relative to the center of the 3D Window. Unit | Set unit for placement. * As shown in the image below, the Add Avatar function can load and use human-shaped Avatars, as well as parts needed for production, such as helmets, shoulder pads, armor and petticoats. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438529090969) * When using multiple Avatars, save as Project file to save all Avatars (ver2.3.0).

title: Cache Animation Export
content: ### Objective Export Animation cache data. ※ Note: Only the cache data related to the Garment can be exported. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation * Maya Cache (.mc) * Maya Cache (.mcx) * Point Cache 2 * MDD Cache (Standard) * MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max) Operation * Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation ● Maya Cache (.mc) ● Maya Cache (.mcx) ● Point Cache 2 ● MDD Cache(Standard) ● MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max) → The Save File window appears. * Select the desired file and click OK. → The Export window opens. Set the full details and click OK. Object | Single Object Exports the selected object as a single object. | Multiple Objects Exports the selected object as multiple objects. ---|---|--- UnWeld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0. (ver2.3.0). | Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. ※Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. | Image File | Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: ‘File Name_0’, ‘File Name_1’. ---|--- Texture Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. Scale | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from “Unit in file to import” is selected. Axis Conversion | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation | Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) | Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) File | * Save With Texture Files (.zip): Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. * Save with Meta Data (.xml) : Export the garment's pattern (Mesh), physical property, and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). * Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: Combine and save the garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). * Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo): Exclude the Ambient color value when saving materials (ver2.2.0).
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide for exporting animation cache data related to garments, detailing the steps, file formats, and options available for effective data management.

title: Guide for Installing Network Offline Version on the Internet Environment
content: ### Guide for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment ### Objective Set up Marvelous Designer/Marvelous Designer Network Version on the Internet environment. Note that you do not need to follow the set-up guidelines below when a Server PC and Client PC are under the same local network environment. Simply plugging the dongle key into a Server PC enables you to run Marvelous Designer or Marvelous Designer on any PCs under the same local network as the Server PC located without any extra settings. ### 1.) Set-up on Server PC ### Operation #### 1\. Plug the dongle key in the Server PC and install the HASP Driver. HASP Driver gets automatically installed during the software installation. However if any trouble occurs during the process or in case of Server only being connected with the dongle key, HASP Driver should be installed manually. #### [Guideline for Sentinel HASP Driver Manual Installation ](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358254274585) 2\. Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall. Port 1947 should be automatically opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. #### 3\. Make sure the local IP address of the Server is static. (Local IP is dynamically allocated Intranet IP by the router.) The local IP address gets changed when the router is restarted if the local IP is not set in static status. To avoid repetitive IP reset in the process, 'port forwarding', set your Server's local IP as 'static'. #### 4\. Port-forward Port 1947 for TCP and UDP of the Server's local IP in the router setting. Port-forwarding enables to transmit the data from Client/Server to Server/Client through Port 1947. Port-forwarding method vary considerably in the types of router therefore please ask for support from your network manager. ※ Note: [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_forwarding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_forwarding) [http://www.wikihow.com/Set-up-Port-Forwarding-on-a-Router](https://www.wikihow.com/Set-Up-Port-Forwarding-on-a-Router) ### ### 2.) Set-up on Client PC ### Operation 1\. Run Marvelous Designer/Marvelous Designer Network Version installer. 2\. Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall. Port 1947 should automatically be opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and the dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. 3\. Set external IP of the Server on the dongle key configuration to let the software reaches the Server for an authentication. This can be done through Sentinel Admin Control Center which is automatically installed during the HASP Driver installation. Access to [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) Click on 'Configuration' (the red box) ![3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438789862425) 4\. Click on the third tab, which is called, 'Access to Remote License Managers'. ![2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438790034457) 5\. Make sure to check on 'Aggressive Search for Remote License' and to type the Server PC's external IP in 'Specify Search Parameters' (note that the external IP is different from the local IP mentioned in the 'Set-up on Server PC'). You are able to see the external IP of the Server PC on the website ([http://www.whatismyip.com/](https://www.whatismyip.com/)). ![1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438796362137)
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for setting up the Marvelous Designer Network Version in an Internet environment, detailing essential steps for both Server and Client PCs to ensure proper installation and communication.

title: Windows - Certificate Authentication Issues After Installation
content: ### Objective How to resolve certificate authentication issues after installation in Windows. ### Operation #### OPTION1 ※Note: Please make sure to download both certificate files from the links below to allow the program to run properly. The certification files are attached at the bottom of the page. 1. Click on the link to [download](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358389230233) the Certificate_1(certificate.crt) / Certificate_2(IntermediateCA.crt) file. 2. Navigate to the folder where the Certificate file was downloaded. 3. Right-click on the Certificate file, then click on Install Certificate. ![Windows_Install_error_1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438683745305) ▲ Certificate.crt ![Windows_Install_error_2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438683846169) ▲ IntermediateCA.crt 4. Select Local Machine, then click Next. ![Windows_Install_error_3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438684059289) 5. Select Place all certificates in the following store then click Browse... ![Windows_Install_error_4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438684252825) 6. Click on Show physical stores at the bottom of the window. 7. Expand the Trusted Root Certification Authorities folder. 8. Click on Registry, then click OK. ![Windows_Install_error_5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438728453785) 9. Click Next. 10. Review the information, then click Finish. ![Windows_Install_error_6.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438728615833) 11. The import was successful message appears, then click OK. 12. Start the program. #### OPTION 2 ※ Note: Should OPTION 1 fail to solve the issue, please use OPTION 2. 1. Download the Certificate_1 (certificate.crt) / Certificate_2 (IntermediateCA.crt)/ Certificate_3(china-certificate.crt) file attached below. 2. Click on the Start button, then run CMD. ![Windows_Install_error_7.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438728752921) 3. In the command prompt, input cd _location of the downloaded certificate file_ , then press Enter on the keyboard. ![Windows_Install_error_8.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438684972569) ※ Note: Path Cannot be Located Issue Confirm if there is a space after cd Confirm that the file path to where the downloaded file is located is correct. 4. In the command prompt, input "certutil -addstore -user -f root certificate.crt" / "certutil -addstore -user -f root IntermediateCA.crt"/ "certutil -addstore -user -f root china-certificate.crt" then press Enter on the keyboard. ![Windows_Install_error_9.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438685141273) ![Windows_Install_error_10.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438729296665) ![Windows_Install_error_11.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438685497881) 5. Start the program again.
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions to resolve certificate authentication issues in Windows following installation.

title: Avatar Skin Offset Setting
content: ### Objective Avatar Skin Offset refers to the distance between the avatar's body and garments. As the avatars and garments are composed of mesh, the avatar's body may penetrate and show through garments if the avatar's Skin Offset is low (when the distance between avatar's body and garments is close) and the Particle Distance is large. To prevent this, the avatar's default Skin Offset is set to 3mm, which is suitable for garment production. Lower the Skin Offset value for precise fitting measurement or for detailed Simulations when producing form-fitting garments. ※ Note: Lowering the Skin Offset lowers the Particle Distance to prevent penetration of garments and also lowers the Simulation speed. It is preferable to keep the default value when working on the garments and once it is done, lower the value and Particle Distance together for fit checking or to use it as an image. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ▶ Skin Offset ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ▶ Skin Offset 2. Enter desired value between 0~100. 3. Click Simulate to simulate according to the set value.
content_description: This webpage provides a guide for adjusting the Avatar Skin Offset in 3D garment production to ensure proper fitting and prevent garment penetration.

title: Camera Setting
content: ### Objective Edit Camera Properties using 3D window view. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Camera Properties ▶ Default Camera Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ Camera (ver 11) Right-click Pop-up Menu (3D window) ▶ Camera Properties ▶ Default Camera Object Browser ▶ Scene ▶ Root ▶ 3D Simulation ▶ Default Camera ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: → The Camera properties display in the Property Editor. 2\. Adjust the default values according to the needs. Lens | View Orientation | Clip Plane ---|---|--- Field of View | Sets view range by adjusting Camera Lens Field of View. | Type | Selects the view type between Spherical or Absolute. | Near | Assigns the nearest distance camera can capture. | Spherical (Object centered) | Distance | Adjusts camera view distance to zoom in and out. | Far | Assigns the farthest distance camera can Horizontal Angle | Rotates camera view to horizontal. | Vertical Angle | Rotates camera view to vertical. Absolute (X,Y centered) | Horizontal Shift | Locates objects to horizontal. Vertical Shift | Locates objects to vertical.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing camera properties in a 3D window view, enabling users to customize lens settings, view orientation, and clipping planes to optimize their visual experience.

title: Segment Darts
content: ### Objective Add or modify Darts located along Pattern outlines. ### Location #### Create Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Point) ▶ Add Dart #### Edit Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) ▶ Edit Dart ### Operation #### Create 1. Choose the Edit pattern (Z) tool from the 2D toolbar and click on the point which a Dart should be added. → The clicked point is selected and highlighted in yellow. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below. Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Point) ▶ Add Dart → The Dart window appears. 3. Adjust the below options as needed and click OK. Name | Description ---|--- Total Width | Set the total horizontal length of a Dart. Dart Arm Width | Set 1/2 of the horizontal length of a Dart. Length | Set the depth of a Dart. → The Dart is created based on the above settings. #### Edit 1. Choose the Edit pattern (Z) tool from the 2D toolbar and select Pattern outlines that form the Dart. → The segments are selected and highlighted in yellow. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below. Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) ▶ Edit Dart → The Dart window appears. 3. Similarly, adjust the options in the Dart window and select OK. → Any modified settings are reflected on the Dart.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adding or modifying Darts along Pattern outlines using the Edit pattern tool and context-specific right-click pop-up menus.

title: Press
content: ### Objective Use this function to create pressing effect especially for the edges of two layers sewn together. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Press 3D Toolbar ▶ Press ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Press 3D Toolbar ▶ Press 2. Click on one of the Pattern layers to press. → The selected Pattern is now being transparent. 3. Click on the other layer. → All Sewing Lines on the selected Pattern switched to Turned Sewing Line Type (ver4.1.0). → The Pattern selected first appears again. 4. Activate the Simulate. → The bulging edges are now being flattened.
content_description: "Utilize this tool to achieve a realistic pressing effect on the edges of sewn layers in your 3D garment designs."

title: Reset 3D Arrangement
content: ### Objective Return arrangement of the entire or selected Patterns back to pre-simulation state in the 3D window. Use this function when draping is not functioning properly after arranging around the Avatar. ### Location #### Selected Pattern 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected) #### All Pattern Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Reset 3D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar ▶ Reset 3D Arrangement (All) ### Operation #### Selected Pattern 1. Select a 3D Pattern to reset its arrangement. ※ Note: Press the Shift key on keyboard to select multiple Patterns. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected) → The selected Pattern is now being rearranged back to pre-simulation state. #### All Pattern 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Reset 3D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar ▶ Reset 3D Arrangement (All) → The entire Pattern is now being rearranged back to pre-simulation state.

title: 3D M:N Segment Sewing (VER4.2.0)
content: ### Objective In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ M:N Segment Sewing ※ Note: Hold down the Segment Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Segment Sewing tool. ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ M:N Segment Sewing 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ M:N Segment Sewing → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. → M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. 3. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. ※ Note: * While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment. ※ Note: 3D Sewing Video
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide on how to efficiently sew multiple segments together in both 2D and 3D environments using the M:N Segment Sewing tool, highlighting key operations and features for optimal user experience.

title: MODULAR MODE: Open/Save Blocks
content: ### Objective Open and save Block component files (.ZBLC). ### Location Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor ### Operation Open 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 2.Mouse over on a desired Modular Template. → Open button appears. 3\. Click Open button to load Block files. Save 1.Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ Block Editor 2\. Mouse over on a desired Modular Template. → Save button appears. 3\. Click Save button. → A pop-up window appears. 4\.
